routes.description: Defend the evidential force of Grim Reaper paradoxes for causal finitism through a warranted modal-independence principle, while arguing that suffering does not favor indifference once consciousness, background knowledge, human epistemic limits, and morally valuable features of finite life are included.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the modal bridge from a possible infinite causal past to the contradictory arrangement survives the recombination objections, and if the existence and distribution of suffering are shown to be no more expected under indifference than under a suitably specified perfect-being theism.

motionBridge.description: Establish both that Grim Reaper reasoning provides support for causal finitism and that suffering does not yield the proposed comparative advantage for indifference over theism.

centralBridges.description: Justify the conditional from a possible infinite causal history, together with independently variable clock settings, to the possibility of the contradictory Grim Reaper configuration.
Fix the relevant background knowledge and compare how theism and indifference account for consciousness, suffering generally, and the particular observed forms of suffering.

Show how limited human access to divine reasons and goods involving risk, relationship, growth, and finite agency can make unexplained suffering compatible with the expectations of perfect-being theism.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish adjacent-world variation of jointly existing objects from unrestricted infinite recombination and explain why the former retains evidential force.
Supply a morally relevant account of divine permission, including the possible roles of consent, compensation, responsibility, and world-level goods.

routes.description: Block the inference from Grim Reaper contradictions to causal finitism by locating the inconsistency in the arrangement rather than the infinite past, while defending the modest likelihood claim that severe apparently gratuitous suffering is more expected under indifference than under bare perfect-being theism.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if an infinite causal past need not license the paradoxical recombination and the minimal inconsistency diagnosis is adequate, and if the observed severity and distribution of suffering remain comparatively less expected under theism after the proposed background assumptions and theodicies are examined.

motionBridge.description: Establish both that Grim Reaper paradoxes do not support causal finitism and that observed suffering supplies comparative evidence favoring indifference over perfect-being theism.

centralBridges.description: Show that rejecting only the jointly inconsistent Grim Reaper conditions blocks the paradox without requiring rejection of every infinite causal history.
Demonstrate that infinite recombination and proximity intuitions do not reliably transmit possibility to the paradoxical total configuration.
Show that the severity, apparent gratuity, and unequal distribution of suffering lower its expected probability under bare perfect-being theism relative to indifference.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain why the logically minimal inconsistency diagnosis is preferable to adding a substantive causal-finitist restriction when both exclude the paradox.
Test whether skeptical-theist and purpose-specific explanations have independent grounding and preserve meaningful confirmation and disconfirmation by worldly evidence.

sections.title: Grim Reaper Contradiction and the Causal-Finitist Inference
sections.rationale: This issue contains the direct motion-level dispute over whether the contradiction warrants rejecting an infinite causal past or only the jointly unsatisfiable features of the proposed arrangement.

sections.title: Modal Independence, Recombination, and Possibility
sections.rationale: The causal-finitist argument depends on a defensible transition from possible components or nearby configurations to the possibility of the infinite paradoxical whole.

sections.title: Comparative Likelihoods and Evidential Background
sections.rationale: The suffering dispute turns on how theism and indifference predict consciousness, suffering in general, and its specific observed forms once shared background knowledge and auxiliary commitments are fixed.

sections.title: Unknown Reasons, Moral Knowledge, and Evidential Symmetry
sections.rationale: Appeals to cognitive limitation must be weighed against ordinary moral knowledge and the concern that unrestricted unknown-purpose explanations neutralize evidence both against and for divine goodness.

sections.title: Theodicies and the Severity and Distribution of Suffering
sections.rationale: Consent, compensation, finite-agent goods, relationships, and world-level value must address not merely suffering's possibility but its extreme cases, unequal allocation, and apparently better alternatives.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: If a possible infinite causal past would permit the contradictory Grim Reaper arrangement, the impossibility of that arrangement supports the conclusion that the causal past is finite.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: If an infinite past were possible, independently randomized clock settings could realize the Grim Reaper sequence, supporting the disputed possibility conditional.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: The Grim Reaper paradox supports causal finitism through the form: if an infinite past is possible, the setup is possible; the setup is impossible; therefore an infinite past is impossible.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: Varying intrinsic settings of clocks that already coexist in one possible world is categorically different from recombining infinitely many objects drawn from separate possible worlds.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-02.proposition: A consequence entailed by theism does not lower that hypothesis's prior probability, whereas adding conscious sufferers to bare indifference may require an independent probability-lowering auxiliary assumption.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: Finite thinkers should expect not to know many of an infinite mind's reasons if theism is true, so ignorance of a reason for suffering is only weak evidence against theism.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-09.proposition: A commonsense intuition that God would have prevented a particular evil can provide reasonable justification even without a stronger supporting philosophical argument.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-10.proposition: God's creation of an arena may differ morally from wrongdoing within it when embodied beings voluntarily accept risks for opportunities involving growth, love, lessons, and experience.

chunk-005:chunk-005-candidate-02.proposition: A world of diverse finite agents can realize goods of growth, relationship, discovery, risk, delegated responsibility, and collective progress unavailable in a world containing only maximally great beings.

chunk-005:chunk-005-candidate-03.proposition: Without restrictive background assumptions, theism provides resources for conscious, adventuresome life and suffering may therefore be more probable on theism than indifference, although specific suffering and richer background knowledge can reverse the comparison.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Causal finitism is unnecessary because the unsatisfiable-pair diagnosis blocks the paradox by rejecting only the contradictory combination.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Because both diagnoses exclude the paradox equally well, parsimony favors the logically minimal unsatisfiable-pair account over causal finitism.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: Ordinary rearrangement can cross from possibility into logical impossibility, so recombination intuitions do not by themselves preserve possibility.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: Infinite recombination is epistemically unreliable, normally caveated, and cannot transfer the impossibility of a joint configuration to either component alone.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: Apparently unnecessary suffering is more expected under indifference than under perfect theism and therefore provides modest evidence favoring indifference.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: No quantity of compensating benefit automatically makes deliberately causing or permitting atrocities morally acceptable, because some harms resist an aggregative ledger of goods and evils.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-08.proposition: Shared moral knowledge in clear cases permits judging that permitting torture is wrong regardless of compensating goods, and many actual sufferings appear relevantly similar to those cases.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-09.proposition: A theism compatible with every possible observation becomes unfalsifiable and cannot connect worldly events strongly enough to rationally affect belief.

chunk-005:chunk-005-candidate-01.proposition: A world that requires some people to endure extreme deprivation for others' flourishing would distribute suffering unfairly and callously.

chunk-005:chunk-005-candidate-04.proposition: Although consciousness in the abstract may initially appear more likely on theism, its precarious dependence on alterable brain matter fits an accidental natural process better than deliberate divine production.
